IR.rationale: A rise in intermediate yields relative to the policy rate, without a matching rise in bill rates, points to a term-premium shock rather than a policy shock. Term-premium shocks tend to partly reverse, which raises expected bond returns afterwards.

B.rationale: Easy credit conditions (strong high-yield returns, stable high-grade spreads) capture the risk-on/risk-off state. That state drives flight-to-quality flows into and out of Treasuries and investment-grade bonds.

V.rationale: Broad high uncertainty across equity and commodity options raises the hedging demand for safe government bonds. It is associated with lower yields and positive bond returns afterwards.

AP.rationale: Equity performance summarises the growth and risk-appetite news that moves yields through the stock-bond correlation.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to subsequent Treasury returns.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength reflects relative US rate rises and capital inflows. It tends to precede some reversal in US yields.

COM.rationale: Oil price gains feed headline inflation expectations and push nominal yields up, which hurts bond returns.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with falling inflation compensation describe a disinflationary risk-off state. That state favours duration through lower expected policy rates.

ENDG.rationale: Recent bond returns capture short-horizon momentum or reversal in yields.

IR.rationale: A bear steepening, with long and intermediate yields rising relative to short rates, signals term-premium repricing. Such repricing tends to cluster and raises subsequent rate volatility.

B.rationale: Weak risky-credit returns signal deteriorating risk appetite. This brings large flight-to-quality and deleveraging flows that raise future Treasury volatility.

V.rationale: High option-implied volatility in gold and equities captures elevated macro and real-rate uncertainty. That uncertainty spills over into bond-market volatility beyond its own lagged variance.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs are followed by higher volatility across asset classes, including safe-haven bonds.

ST.rationale: Style factors have no clear mechanism for bond volatility.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation reflects global funding pressure and shifts in rate differentials. Both are associated with more turbulent rate markets.

COM.rationale: Commodity returns carry little incremental information on bond variance once volatility indices are included.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with high measured financial stress predict elevated volatility across fixed-income markets.

ENDG.rationale: Recent bond variance relative to its own history captures volatility mean reversion beyond persistence.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening, with long and intermediate yields rising faster than policy rates, signals a term-premium shock. Such shocks can extend into a large duration sell-off.

B.rationale: Weak EM sovereign dollar-bond returns flag global rate and dollar-funding pressure. That pressure can spill into US yields through reserve-manager selling.

V.rationale: High gold volatility reflects uncertainty about real rates and inflation, which is the main driver of large bond losses.

AP.rationale: Value outperformance accompanies reflation and rising yields. It marks the regime in which bond sell-offs are most likely.

ST.rationale: Momentum and quality underperforming together indicate a rotation toward cyclical, rate-sensitive stocks. That rotation is consistent with rising yields.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar against the euro often reflects rising foreign yields and reduced foreign demand for Treasuries. Both raise the risk of a US bond sell-off.

COM.rationale: A broad commodity rally led by oil raises inflation expectations and nominal yields, increasing the chance of large bond losses.

MC.rationale: Stress that coincides with rising inflation compensation is rate-driven stress, not flight to quality. In that case bonds are the source of losses rather than the hedge.

ENDG.rationale: Recent strong bond returns leave yields stretched, making a subsequent large reversal more likely.

IR.rationale: Falling bill rates signal expected policy easing or flight to safety. Both precede strong duration rallies.

B.rationale: The state of credit conditions, from calm high-grade spreads to strong junk returns, distinguishes risk-on regimes from risk-off regimes. Risk-off regimes produce outsized safe-haven bond gains.

V.rationale: Elevated equity and oil uncertainty raises safe-haven demand and growth fears, setting up large Treasury rallies.

AP.rationale: Equity momentum summarises growth and risk-appetite news, which determines whether flight-to-quality bond rallies occur.

ST.rationale: Style factors have no clear link to large bond gains.

FX.rationale: Carry-currency strength reflects stretched risk-on positioning. Its unwinding is associated with sharp moves into safe bonds.

COM.rationale: Precious-metal strength reflects falling real-rate expectations, which accompany bond rallies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise the odds of policy easing and flight to quality, which produce large bond gains.

ENDG.rationale: Recent bond returns capture trend persistence or exhaustion of rallies at short horizons.
